originalTitle: Family of Irish plane crash victim awarded $29m in damages
summary: A jury in Chicago in the US awarded the sum to Michael Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against Boeing.
content:
Michael Ryan was among the 157 people killed on board the Ethiopian Airlines plane

The widow of an Irish United Nations employee, who died in 2019 following a Boeing 737 Max crash in Ethiopia, has been awarded $29m (£21.5m) in damages.

A jury in Chicago in the United States awarded the sum to Michael 'Mick' Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against the aircraft manufacturer.

Her lawyers have said the verdict "represents an important measure of accountability and justice".

A Boeing spokesperson said the company is "deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones" and they "respect" the right for families to "pursue their claims".

Michael Ryan, a father of two living in Cork but originally from County Clare, was among the 157 people killed on board the Ethiopian Airlines plane.

He had worked as an engineer with the United Nations World Food Programme.

Lawyer Steven C Marks, who represented Ryan's widow, said: "While no financial award can ever replace a life or undo the profound loss his family has endured, we are grateful that the jury carefully considered the evidence and reached this decision."

Marks said that Connolly Ryan has "pursued justice for Mick with extraordinary strength and determination" and his firm Podhurst Orseck have been "honoured to stand beside her in her unwavering pursuit to hold Boeing accountable".

"Although the verdict marks a significant milestone, the broader effort to hold Boeing responsible for this tragedy, and to help prevent anything like it from happening again, is just as important," he added.

In a statement, a Boeing spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones on Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302.

"While we have resolved nearly all of these claims through settlements, families are entitled to pursue their claims through the court process, and we respect their right to do so."

Lawyer Steven Marks says Ryan's family have pursued justice with "extraordinary strength"

On a United Nations memorial page to Michael Ryan , external it said he helped the World Food Programme "bring assistance to vulnerable people" in Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Ethiopia and Bangladesh.

The organisation credits him with organising "the building of shelters and infrastructure" in Bangladesh "which saved tens of thousands of Rohingya refugees from the threat of landslides and floods".

It also said he built medical centres in Liberia during the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak.

Marks told BBC News NI that Ryan "will be missed by the world at large" as that was "who he served".

"It's tragic to the public, but it pales in comparison to the loss for the family.

What happened to Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 Max?

Relatives pay their respects to those who died in the Ethiopian Airlines crash

Flight ET302 took off from Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa at 08:38 local time (05:38 GMT) on 10 March for a two-hour flight to the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.

Six minutes later, at 08:44, it crashed 30 miles southeast of the airport , near the town of Bishoftu.

The impact was so great, both engines were buried at a depth of 10m (32ft), in a crater 28m wide and 40m long.

The preliminary report into the accident, by Ethiopia's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, said the plane's take-off appeared normal.

However, a short time later two sensors that measured the angle of the plane's flight began to record different readings.

This triggered an automated safety system which repeatedly pushed the nose of the plane down - something that was also recorded during the fatal Lion Air flight.

The Ethiopian authorities' 2019 report suggested the pilots followed steps to disengage the system, but even after manually trying to steady the plane, the system pushed the nose down until the aircraft crashed.

chineseTitle: 爱尔兰空难受害者家属获赔 2900 万美元
chineseSummary: 在迈克尔·瑞安（Michael Ryan）的遗孀纳伊丝·康诺利·瑞安（Naoise Connolly Ryan）对波音公司提起民事诉讼后，美国芝加哥陪审团将这笔款项判给了迈克尔·瑞安的家人。
chineseContent:
迈克尔·瑞安 (Michael Ryan) 是埃塞俄比亚航空公司客机上 157 名遇难者之一

一名爱尔兰联合国雇员于 2019 年在埃塞俄比亚波音 737 Max 坠机事故中丧生，她的遗孀获得了 2900 万美元（2150 万英镑）的赔偿。

在迈克尔·“米克”·瑞安的遗孀 Naoise Connolly Ryan 对飞机制造商提起民事诉讼后，美国芝加哥的一个陪审团将这笔赔偿金判给了迈克尔·“米克”·瑞安的家人。

她的律师表示，这一判决“代表了问责和正义的重要举措”。

波音发言人表示，该公司“对所有失去亲人的人深感抱歉”，并“尊重”家属“寻求索赔”的权利。

迈克尔·瑞安 (Michael Ryan) 是两个孩子的父亲，居住在科克，但来自克莱尔郡，他是埃塞俄比亚航空公司飞机上遇难的 157 人之一。

他曾在联合国世界粮食计划署担任工程师。

瑞安遗孀的代表律师史蒂文·C·马克斯表示：“虽然任何经济赔偿都无法取代生命，也无法挽回他家人所遭受的巨大损失，但我们很感激陪审团仔细考虑了证据并做出了这一决定。”

马克斯表示，康诺利·瑞安“以非凡的力量和决心为米克伸张正义”，而他的公司 Podhurst Orseck 也“很荣幸能站在她身边，坚定不移地追究波音的责任”。

他补充说：“尽管这一判决标志着一个重要的里程碑，但让波音公司对这场悲剧负责并帮助防止类似事件再次发生的更广泛努力也同样重要。”

波音发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们对所有在狮航 610 航班和埃塞俄比亚航空 302 航班上失去亲人的人深感抱歉。

“虽然我们已经通过和解解决了几乎所有这些索赔，但家庭有权通过法庭程序提出索赔，我们尊重他们这样做的权利。”

律师史蒂文·马克斯表示，瑞安的家人以“非凡的力量”追求正义

联合国在迈克尔·瑞安的纪念页面上对外表示，他帮助世界粮食计划署在阿富汗、斯里兰卡、尼泊尔、埃塞俄比亚和孟加拉国“为弱势群体提供援助”。

该组织称赞他在孟加拉国组织了“庇护所和基础设施建设”，“使数以万计的罗兴亚难民免受山体滑坡和洪水的威胁”。

它还说他在2014-16年埃博拉疫情爆发期间在利比里亚建立了医疗中心。

马克斯告诉英国广播公司新闻NI，瑞安“将被全世界怀念”，因为“他所服务的人”。

“这对公众来说是一场悲剧，但与家庭的损失相比就显得苍白无力了。

埃塞俄比亚航空波音 737 Max 发生了什么事？

亲属悼念埃塞俄比亚航空空难中的遇难者

3月10日当地时间08:38（格林威治标准时间05:38）ET302航班从埃塞俄比亚首都亚的斯亚贝巴起飞，飞行两个小时飞往肯尼亚首都内罗毕。

六分钟后，即 08:44，飞机在机场东南 30 英里处坠毁，地点靠近 Bishoftu 镇。

冲击力如此之大，两台发动机都被埋在 10m（32 英尺）深、宽 28m、长 40m 的陨石坑中。

埃塞俄比亚飞机事故调查局对事故的初步报告称，飞机的起飞似乎正常。

然而，不久之后，测量飞机飞行角度的两个传感器开始记录不同的读数。

这触发了自动安全系统，反复将飞机机头向下推——这一情况在狮航致命航班中也被记录下来。

埃塞俄比亚当局 2019 年的报告建议飞行员按照步骤脱离该系统，但即使在手动尝试稳定飞机后，系统仍将机头向下推，直到飞机坠毁。
